Encord releases EMG-1 with over 300 hours of muscle signals and video

The Wearable Devices collaboration targets hand tracking under occlusion alongside the launch of Data Labs and the REACH tracking model.

PR Newswire ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Another signal for learning manipulation

Encord released EMG-1 with Wearable Devices on October 20. It contains over 300 hours of synchronized forearm electromyography, first-person video and optical motion capture. The open dataset is intended to help researchers develop robot movement and object-manipulation learning.

Tracking when cameras lose the fingers

Objects being handled often hide fingers from cameras. Wristbands add EMG signals associated with finger movement to the visual stream. Encord reports 25% lower fingertip-position error and 35% lower error during brief visual gaps. These are company tracking evaluations, not success rates across all robotic tasks.

A lab and tracking tools launch together

The release accompanies Encord Data Labs and REACH, a hand-tracking model for gloves, obscured fingers, fast motion and multiple hands. These efforts improve training-data quality. Adding muscle signals does not by itself guarantee that a trained robot can regulate force or handle every situation autonomously.
